mithi.name: Mithi catchment
mithi.coverage: CPCB Polluted River Stretches report, October 2025 (station 2168) + MPCB Water Quality Status reports 2018-19 to 2023-24 + Praja Foundation 2024 (RTI series on BMC's plants) + BMC ESR 2024-25 + NGT OA 150/2025 as reported
mithi.headline: CPCB's October 2025 assessment puts the Mithi at station 2168 at a maximum BOD of 210 mg/l, the highest of any polluted river stretch in India. At its head about 18 MLD of untreated sewage enters Powai Lake, and the 8 MLD plant meant to stop it is not to be commissioned before December 2027.
caveats: CPCB lists one monitoring location on the Mithi (station 2168, near the road bridge at Mahim); nothing on the river above it is monitored by CPCB or MPCB in the sources compiled here. The 2019 MPCB action plan sampled 16 points once.
The 2023 faecal-coliform figure (540,000 MPN/100 ml, a 100x jump from 2022) is CPCB's published value; Praja, transcribing the same series, flags it as a likely recording error. Directional only.

Who holds what: BMC's Hydraulic Engineer's Department for supply and the Mumbai Sewerage Disposal Project for treatment; MPCB for monitoring, consents and the 2019 action plan; the Mithi River Development and Protection Authority (2005) for the widening and wall works, executed by BMC and MMRDA.

streams.summary: The worst-reading river stretch in the country, with the untreated inflow at Powai Lake fixed on the NGT record until December 2027.

metrics.label: Worst CPCB reading
metrics.value: BOD 210 mg/l maximum in 2022-23, 80 mg/l in 2024, at station 2168 (CPCB, October 2025); the bathing criterion is 3 mg/l

metrics.label: MPCB annual averages, station 2168
metrics.value: BOD 45.3 mg/l (2018-19) to 53.0 (2023-24), the worst year in the series; dissolved oxygen 2.2 to 4.1 mg/l; Water Quality Index 32 (2023-24)

metrics.label: Raw sewage into Powai Lake
metrics.value: About 18 MLD (BMC's affidavit says about 10.9) until the 8 MLD STP is commissioned, not before 11 December 2027 (NGT OA 150/2025)

metrics.label: Treatment in this catchment
metrics.value: Powai waste stabilisation pond, 8 MLD (MPCB inventory)

metrics.label: Restoration
metrics.value: Powai Lake Restoration, about Rs 66 crore (2025): the 8 MLD STP, sewage diversion (8 MLD to Bhandup, about 2 MLD to a Mithi STP) and hyacinth removal

metrics.label: River works
metrics.value: Mithi widening 93.96% and retaining walls 94.60% complete at 30 April 2025, two decades after the 2005 deluge (BMC ESR 2024-25)

sources.says: River Mithi near road bridge, Mahim: Priority I, maximum BOD 210 mg/l (2022-23); station 2168 BOD 80 mg/l in 2024. Same class as in 2018 (Powai to Dharavi, Priority I).

streams.summary: Four of BMC's nine plants fail the 10 mg/l discharge standard; the seven-plant replacement programme has slipped past its own 2026 dates.

metrics.label: Plants failing the discharge standard (2024 outlet BOD)
metrics.value: Malad 99.4 mg/l (140.6 in 2023 against an inlet of 144.2), Versova 58.1, Ghatkopar 24.5, Bhandup 20.7, against the 10 mg/l standard (Praja 2024, Table 13, RTI)

metrics.label: Plants meeting it
metrics.value: Worli (Love Grove) 757 MLD, Bandra 797 MLD, Colaba 41 MLD and Charkop 6 MLD, outlet BOD 1.3 to 5.4 mg/l in 2023-24; Worli and Bandra were offline in 2024 for reconstruction

metrics.label: Installed capacity
metrics.value: About 2,735 MLD across the nine BMC plants in MPCB's inventory (Worli 757, Bandra 797, Ghatkopar 386, Malad 280, Bhandup 280, Versova 180, Colaba 41, Powai 8, Charkop 6)

metrics.label: MSDP-2 replacement programme
metrics.value: Seven plants, 2,464 MLD treated and 1,233 MLD recycled: Worli 500, Malad 454, Dharavi 418, Bandra 360, Ghatkopar 337, Bhandup 215, Versova 180 MLD. Progress 25-43% per plant at 30 April 2025; completion 2026 (three plants), 2027 (three), 2028 (Malad)

metrics.label: Dates already missed
metrics.value: Versova and Ghatkopar were due 4 July 2026 and Bhandup 22 August 2026 by BMC's own ESR table; all three stand as slipped in the commitments register

dahisar.name: Dahisar catchment
dahisar.coverage: CPCB Polluted River Stretches report, October 2025 (absence) + MPCB Water Quality Status reports (absence) + MPCB per-STP inventory
dahisar.headline: Not in CPCB's national list and not monitored as a river: what reaches the Dahisar is undocumented in every source compiled here, and there is no treatment plant in its catchment.
caveats: Absence from CPCB's list is absence from monitoring, not evidence of clean water: the river is a sewage-fed channel through built-up Dahisar (MPCB and CPCB descriptions carried in the city river file).
BMC's river-rejuvenation programme names the Dahisar (STPs under trial in 2025); no capacity or performance figure for those works is published in the sources compiled here.

streams.summary: Undocumented: no station, no inlet survey, no plant.

oshiwara.name: Oshiwara catchment
oshiwara.coverage: CPCB Polluted River Stretches report, October 2025 (absence) + MPCB Water Quality Status reports (absence) + MPCB per-STP inventory + Praja 2024 + BMC ESR 2024-25
oshiwara.headline: Malad Creek, which the Oshiwara joins, takes the outflow of the Malad (280 MLD) and Versova (180 MLD) plants. Malad's 2023 outlet BOD of 140.6 mg/l against an inlet of 144.2 means the plant barely treats; its 454 MLD replacement is the last of the programme, due 2028.
caveats: Absence from CPCB's list is absence from monitoring, not evidence of clean water: the river is heavily encroached and sewage-fed through Goregaon and Jogeshwari.
The Malad and Versova plants discharge to the creek system the Oshiwara drains into, not to the river itself; their figures are the creek's load, not a river reading.
